question: The Supreme Court has special advisory jurisdiction in matters which may specifically be referred to it by the President of India under Article ____ of the Constitution.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 143**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article **143** of the **Indian Constitution** grants the **Supreme Court of India** special advisory jurisdiction in matters specifically referred to it by the **President of India**. 
 
• The President can seek the Supreme Court's opinion on questions of law or fact that arise out of public importance, 
 
 
• and the Court may offer its advisory opinion in such cases.
 
 
 
• This power allows the President to consult the highest judicial authority for guidance on constitutional matters and other significant legal issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 141**:

 
 
• **States that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.**
 
• It **Promotes consistency in the application of laws and ensures the supremacy of the Supreme Court as the interpreter of the Constitution.**
 
• This ensures uniformity in the interpretation of laws across the country.
 
• The judgments of the Supreme Court set precedents that lower courts must follow (Doctrine of Precedent).
 
 
 
• **Article 142**:
 
 
• Grants the Supreme Court the power to pass any order or decree for doing complete justice in any case.
 
• **This article gives the Court extraordinary powers to ensure justice prevails, even in cases where existing laws or technicalities may fall short.**
 
• The Supreme Court has used this article in landmark cases such as:
 
• **Union Carbide Corporation v. Union of India (Bhopal Gas Tragedy case)** to ensure fair compensation.
 
• **Babri Masjid case** for the amicable resolution of disputes.
 
 
 
• **Article 144**:
 
 
• Directs all authorities, civil and judicial, in India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
 
• **This article ensures the enforceability of the Supreme Court’s decisions and directives**.
 
• It mandates that courts and other institutions cooperate with the Supreme Court in administering justice.
